# Hand-written fixtures

Files here are written by hand (or generated by a script that is not kept), not
captured from restic. Each says what it is modelled on. They are replayed by the
agent's fake restic (`internal/agent/internal/fakerestic`) and read by
`internal/restic` tests; `FuzzDecoder` seeds from every file under `testdata`.

## M1-T5

| file | used by | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hostile_paths.stderr.jsonl` | fakerestic scenario `hostile_paths`, `TestT5HostilePathsNeverReachTheConsole` | One restic stderr stream whose lines name files in every shape a path takes: drive letter, UNC, shadow-copy device path, bare quoted names with embedded quotes, a POSIX path, a `\\?\` path with non-ASCII letters, and plain-text lines. The line formats are those of `vss_paths.stderr.jsonl` and `unsupported_file.stderr.jsonl`. Every distinctive token starts with `ZQ7` or is one of `fileserver01`, `Jane`, `GLOBALROOT`; a test greps for them after the stream has gone through the agent and the console. Not a leak of any real machine: every name is invented. |
| `gateway_midrun.stdout.jsonl` | fakerestic scenario `gateway_midrun` | Progress lines of a backup that stalls part-way (the same status repeated). |
| `gateway_midrun.stderr.jsonl` | fakerestic scenario `gateway_midrun` | What restic 0.19.1 prints to stderr, even with `--json`, when the REST gateway disappears mid-upload: its plain-text `Save(<data/..>) returned error, retrying after ..` lines (copied from a real run against a local REST server that was stopped after two packs; host, address and port replaced by reserved example names, the password masked by restic itself as `:***@`), then a final `exit_error` line. **The final line is not captured.** restic 0.19.1 was still retrying the refused connection 30 minutes after the server stopped (lock refreshes included), so no give-up line exists to copy; the line is the shape of restic's `Fatal: unable to save snapshot: <error>` with the error text of the retry lines. Replace it with the real text when one is captured. |
